summary: Gembo Dorji is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Tango Buddhist College, the East-West Center, and the University of Tokyo, alongside traditional teachers including Tenzin Dhendrup and Khamtrul Rinpoche Dongyud Nyima.

Gen'ichi Yamazaki (1935–2015) was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He completed his undergraduate and doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo, later working as a researcher at Toyo Bunko (~1965–1973) and professor at Kokugakuin University (2006).

Gendun Chopel (1903–1951) was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and history. He studied at Drisha, Labrang, Kumbum, and Drepung Monasteries under teachers including Gendun Tendzin Gyatso and Sherab Gyatso.
Gendun Chophel (1903–1952) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Sherab Gyatso from ~1928 to 1934 and held a post at the Maha Bodhi Society in 1941.

Gendun Rinpoche (1918–1997) was a Tibetan Buddhist scholar and teacher. He founded Dhagpo Kundreul Ling, Dhagpo Dedrol Ling, and Dhagpo Kagyu Ling, where he served as abbot and retreat master from ~1977 to 1997.

Genjun Sasaki (1915–1999) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University. He held professorships at the University of Hamburg (1956), Harvard University, and Otani University, and lectured at Osaka University (attested 1995).
Genro Gito (1717–1789) was a Buddhist studies figure who succeeded Hakuin Ekaku and served in the head seat position at Myoshin-ji.
Genryu Kagoshima (1912–2001) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University from ~1932 to 1937. He later served as a professor at Komazawa University from ~1957 to 1983.

Gensho Imanari (1925–2020) specialized in Japanology and Buddhist studies, earning his degrees, including a PhD, at Waseda University. He was an assistant professor at Kokushikan University (~1958–1968) and professor at Rissho University (1980; emeritus in 1996).
Genshu Watanabe (1869–1963) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Toyo University and was a dharma heir under Sogaku Daiun Harada.
Genzao (d. 1993) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Dzogchen Monastery until 1950 and received training under traditional teachers Jiangze Rinpoche and Kalu Rinpoche.

Geo Widengren (1907–1996) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and religion. He studied at Stockholm and Uppsala universities, later serving as professor of religious history at Uppsala (1940–1973) and president of the IAHR (~1960–1970).

Geoff Childs is a scholar of Tibetology and history/anthropology who earned his PhD from Indiana University under Tsetan Chonjore. He held posts at the Australian National University and Washington University in St. Louis.

Geoffrey Barstow is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Hampshire College, Kathmandu University, and the University of Virginia (PhD 2013), and became an assistant professor at Oregon State University around 2013.

Geoffrey Goble is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He earned an MA at the University of Virginia and a PhD at Indiana University, later serving as assistant professor at the University of Oklahoma (attested 2019).

Geoffrey Samuel is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned his PhD at Cambridge under Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah, Peter J. Wilson, and Edmund Leach. He held professorships at Newcastle, Lancaster, and Cardiff universities.

Georg Buddruss (1929–2021) was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Tübingen and Frankfurt under Paul Thieme, and served as professor at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz from 1963 to 1995.

Georg Bühler (1837–1898) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Theodor Benfey at Göttingen. He held posts at Elphinstone College, Deccan College, and the University of Mumbai (~1863–1880), followed by a chair at the University of Vienna.

Georg Christoph Lichtenberg (1742–1799) was a scholar of philosophy and other fields. He studied at the University of Göttingen from ~1763 to 1767 and subsequently held a post there from ~1769 until 1799.

Georg Curtius (1820–1885) was a linguist who studied at Bonn and Berlin under Ritschl, Lassen, and Bopp. He held professorships of classical philology at the universities of Prague (1849–1854), Kiel (1854–1862), and Leipzig (1862–1885).
